_policy: Linthra's reviewed tracker-dependency policy (#504).
scripts/check_tracker_dependencies.py reads this file and compares it
against the identifiers Linthra's production dependency files actually
resolve to: pubspec.lock, the Flatpak pub sources, the Linux plugin
registration, the Android Gradle files and the Rust lockfiles.
Matching is on EXACT identifiers, never on substrings. A Dart entry is a
pub.dev package name; a Maven entry is either a full `group:artifact`
coordinate or, with "match": "group", a whole Maven group; a
gradle-plugin entry is a plugin id; a cargo entry is a crate name. That is
deliberate: a substring rule would flag `audio_amplitude` for Amplitude and
`com.google.firebaseui` for Firebase, and a check that cries wolf gets
switched off.
Every entry carries the reason it is here, so a reviewer can disagree with
a specific line rather than with the list. This is a REVIEW TRIGGER, not a
ban: a match fails CI and asks for a human decision. If the decision is
that the dependency is fine, it is recorded in "exceptions" below.
The list is knowingly incomplete. It names the systems that are widely
deployed enough to be worth naming; it cannot name one nobody has heard of
yet, and it says nothing about code Linthra writes itself. What this check
does and does not prove is written down in
docs/tracker-dependency-audit.md.
Entries are sorted by (ecosystem, identifier) and must be unique. The
checker enforces both, so a hand-edited file cannot drift into an order
that makes review diffs unreadable.
_exceptions: A reviewed exception is a claim that a human looked at a specific match and
decided Linthra should ship the dependency anyway. It is not a way to make
Each entry needs: "ecosystem", the exact "identifier" as the check reports
it, the "sources" the exception covers (the paths the check prints), a
"reason", and "reviewed_in": a link to where the decision was made.
The checker also fails when an exception matches nothing, so a reason can
never outlive the dependency it explains.
Empty is the expected state, and the state PRIVACY.md describes.
